modes.label: Time mode
modes.realtimeHint: Realtime: packets travel at once, like on a real network.
modes.simulationHint: Simulation: time stands still; you step through every packet.

pduTool.pickSource: Simple PDU: click the device that sends the ping.
pduTool.noAddress: {{device}} has no IP address, so there is nothing to ping.
pduTool.sameDevice: Pick another device as the destination.
pduTool.queued: Ping from {{source}} to {{target}} is ready. Press play or step forward.

controls.label: Playback
controls.idle: Nothing is waiting. Send a Simple PDU to start.
controls.exportEmpty: No frames on the wire yet, so there is nothing to export.
controls.skippedSerial_one: {{count}} serial (HDLC) frame is not in the file: a .pcap holds Ethernet frames only.
controls.skippedSerial_other: {{count}} serial (HDLC) frames are not in the file: a .pcap holds Ethernet frames only.

events.label: Event list
events.empty: No events yet. Pick the Simple PDU tool, click two devices, then step forward.
events.filteredEmpty: No event matches the protocol filter.

pdu.none: No PDU (the client gave up waiting)

decisions.buffered: {{device}} holds the PDU until it knows where to send it.
decisions.sent: {{device}} sends the PDU it was holding.
decisions.forwarded: {{device}} forwarded the PDU out of one port.
decisions.flooded: {{device}} copied the PDU out of several ports.
decisions.filtered: {{device}} kept the frame: the destination sits behind the port it came from.
decisions.delivered: {{device}} accepted the PDU: it was meant for this device.
decisions.replied: {{device}} accepted the PDU and is sending an answer.

inspector.label: PDU inspector
inspector.empty: Pick an event in the list or a packet on the map to look inside the device.
inspector.inHint: How the PDU arrived and was unpacked, from the cable upwards.
inspector.outHint: How the PDU was packed and sent, from the top down to the cable.
inspector.noIn: Nothing arrived: this device created the PDU itself.
inspector.noNotes: No decision was noted at this layer.

terminal.stepToAnswer: Waiting for the simulation: press Step forward or Play to get the answer.
terminal.cancelled: The command was cancelled: the simulation was reset or stepped back before it ended.
terminal.preparing: Preparing the simulation… the command runs as soon as it is ready.
terminal.reverted: Stepped back before this command finished: its change to the network (the DHCP address) was undone.

prepare.dormant: The simulation has not started yet: press Start simulation, switch to Simulation or type a command.
prepare.startHint: Build the simulation of this large lab now (it runs in the background; you can keep editing).
prepare.onDemand: This lab has {{count}} devices: the simulation starts only when you need it (Start simulation, Simulation mode or a terminal command).
prepare.truncated: This lab is very large: the start-up traffic was cut short, so the first steps still finish it.

reasons.linkDown: The link does not carry traffic.
reasons.notForThisInterface: The frame is addressed to another device.
reasons.sameSegment: The destination is on the port the frame came from.
reasons.vlanNotAllowed: The VLAN is not allowed on this port.
reasons.vlanInactive: The VLAN does not exist in the VLAN database.
reasons.noSubInterface: No sub-interface for this VLAN tag.
reasons.l2Loop: Layer-2 loop: the frame came back to a switch it already passed.
reasons.arpQueueFull: Too many packets are already waiting for ARP.
reasons.arpNotForUs: The ARP request is for another address.
reasons.unknownSsid: The access point does not offer this SSID.
reasons.ispServiceDown: The internet provider line is down.
reasons.ispNoService: The internet provider serves only routers.
reasons.noEgressPort: No other port can carry the frame: it goes nowhere.
reasons.noDestinationMac: The internet provider answers only the device that asked: no destination MAC.
reasons.invalidHostAddress: The IP address is the network or broadcast address of its subnet.
reasons.ipConflict: Another device uses the same IP address.
reasons.gatewayOutsideSubnet: The default gateway is outside the own network.
reasons.notRouting: The packet is for another address and this device does not route.
reasons.privateToInternet: Private addresses are not routed on the internet.
reasons.ispNoRoute: The internet has no route to this address.
reasons.portUnreachable: No service listens on this port.
reasons.protocolUnreachable: The device does not handle this protocol.
reasons.noIcmpAboutIcmpError: No ICMP error is sent about an ICMP error or a broadcast.
reasons.dhcpNoPool: No DHCP pool for this network.
reasons.dhcpPoolExhausted: The DHCP pool has no free address.
reasons.dhcpNotForThisClient: The DHCP message is for another client.
reasons.dhcpNak: The DHCP server refused the request.
reasons.dnsLoop: The DNS query is already being forwarded (forwarder loop).
reasons.dnsNotAResolver: No DNS server runs at this address.
reasons.aclDenied: An access list on the interface denied the packet.
reasons.natPoolExhausted: NAT has no free address or port left for this packet.
reasons.natNoTranslation: No NAT translation exists for this packet.
reasons.vtyAccessDenied: The remote-access lines refuse this source address (access-class).
reasons.remoteLoginFailed: Remote login failed (user name or password).
reasons.remoteAccessDisabled: Remote access with this protocol is not enabled on the device.
reasons.firewallDenied: The firewall dropped the packet: it goes from a lower security level to a higher one and no access list permits it.
reasons.firewallNoConnection: The firewall dropped the packet: it belongs to no connection the firewall knows.
reasons.firewallSameLevel: The firewall dropped the packet: both interfaces have the same security level and traffic between them is not allowed.
reasons.firewallNoNameif: The firewall dropped the packet: the interface has no name (nameif), so no traffic passes through it.
reasons.staleReply: An answer nobody waits for any more.
reasons.unsupported: The device does not process this PDU.

l1.linkDown: Port {{port}} has no working link: the frame is not sent.
l1.hubRepeats: A hub repeats the signal out of every other port.
l1.noOtherPort: No other port has a working link: the signal goes nowhere.

l2.frameAccepted: The destination MAC {{dst}} belongs to this interface or is a broadcast: the frame is accepted.
l2.notForThisInterface: The destination MAC {{dst}} is not this interface's address: the frame is ignored.
l2.macLearned: The switch learns that {{mac}} is reachable through {{port}} in VLAN {{vlan}}.
l2.macKnown: {{mac}} is in the MAC address table on {{port}}: the frame is forwarded only there.
l2.macUnknown: {{mac}} is not in the MAC address table: the frame is flooded to every port of VLAN {{vlan}}.
l2.broadcastFlooded: Broadcast: the frame is flooded to every port of VLAN {{vlan}} except the one it came from.
l2.sameSegment: The destination was learned on the port the frame came from: it is not forwarded.
l2.accessIngress: Port {{port}} is an access port: the frame belongs to VLAN {{vlan}}.
l2.trunkIngress: Port {{port}} is a trunk: the frame belongs to VLAN {{vlan}}.
l2.taggedEgress: The frame leaves trunk {{port}} with an 802.1Q tag for VLAN {{vlan}}.
l2.vlanNotAllowed: VLAN {{vlan}} is not allowed on port {{port}}: the frame is dropped.
l2.arpRequestCreated: The MAC address of {{ip}} is not in the ARP cache: an ARP request is broadcast.
l2.arpRequestForUs: The ARP request asks for {{ip}}, an address of this interface: an ARP reply is sent.
l2.arpRequestNotForUs: The ARP request asks for {{ip}}, which is not this interface's address: it is ignored.
l2.arpReplyLearned: The ARP reply says {{ip}} is at {{mac}}: the ARP cache is updated.
l2.arpCacheHit: The ARP cache knows that {{ip}} is at {{mac}}.
l2.packetBuffered: The packet waits until ARP resolves {{ip}}.
l2.arpQueueFull: {{limit}} packets already wait for ARP to resolve {{ip}} (the most a next hop holds): this one is dropped.
l2.packetReleased: ARP resolved {{ip}}: the waiting packet is sent.
l2.arpTimeout: No ARP reply from {{ip}} after {{attempts}} attempts: the waiting packets are dropped.
l2.arpProbe: Duplicate address check: an ARP probe asks whether another device uses {{ip}}.
l2.duplicateAddress: Another device answered for {{ip}}: the address is a duplicate and cannot be used.
l2.loopSuppressed: This frame already passed this switch. Without spanning tree it would circle forever, so the lab stops it.
l2.ispServiceDown: The provider line on {{port}} is down: the cloud drops the frame.
l2.deencapsulated: The {{protocol}} payload is handed to the upper layer.
l2.macRefreshed: {{mac}} is already in the MAC address table on {{port}} (VLAN {{vlan}}): its aging timer starts again.
l2.nativeIngress: Untagged frame on trunk {{port}}: it belongs to the native VLAN {{vlan}}.
l2.taggedOnAccess: Access port {{port}} takes only untagged frames; this one carries the 802.1Q tag {{vlan}}, so it is dropped.
l2.ssidIngress: The client is associated with SSID {{ssid}}: its frames belong to VLAN {{vlan}}.
l2.taggedFromClient: Wireless clients send untagged frames; this one carries the tag {{vlan}}, so it is dropped.
l2.radioEgress: The frame goes over the air from {{port}} to the client on SSID {{ssid}}.
l2.floodNoPorts: No other port carries VLAN {{vlan}}: the frame goes nowhere.
l2.sviDelivered: The frame is addressed to the switch itself: interface {{iface}} takes it.
l2.sviCopy: The switch also keeps a copy of the broadcast for its own interface {{iface}}.
l2.sviCopyDiscarded: Interface {{iface}} discards its copy; the frame flooded to the other ports is not affected.
l2.sviEgress: Interface {{iface}} sends into VLAN {{vlan}} through the switch's own ports.
l2.taggedAtNic: A network card does not understand 802.1Q tags: the frame tagged for VLAN {{vlan}} is dropped.
l2.nativeSubInterface: Untagged frame: the native sub-interface {{iface}} takes it.
l2.untaggedRouted: Untagged frame: the physical interface {{iface}} takes it.
l2.interfaceShut: Interface {{iface}} is shut down: the frame is dropped.
l2.encapsulated: The packet goes into an Ethernet frame from {{src}} to {{dst}}.
l2.encapsulatedTagged: Sub-interface {{iface}}: the frame gets the 802.1Q tag {{vlan}}.
l2.hdlcEncapsulated: Serial link: the packet goes into an HDLC frame. A point-to-point link needs no MAC addresses and no ARP.
l2.hdlcReceived: HDLC frame on a serial link: the packet inside is handed to layer 3.
l2.broadcastDestination: The packet is a broadcast: it goes to FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF without ARP.
l2.knownDestination: The destination MAC {{mac}} is already known: no ARP is needed.
l2.arpRetry: Still no ARP reply from {{ip}}: request {{attempt}} of {{attempts}} is broadcast.
l2.arpAlreadyPending: An ARP request for {{ip}} is already on its way: the packet waits with the others.
l2.arpSenderLearned: The request also tells who asks: {{ip}} is at {{mac}}, which goes into the ARP cache.
l2.arpReplyUnsolicited: Nobody here asked for {{ip}}: the reply is ignored.
l2.arpCannotAnswer: {{ip}} is configured here, but a network card does not answer for a network or broadcast address or for a duplicate address.
l2.probeForOurAddress: Another device checks whether {{ip}} is free, but this interface uses it: it answers to defend the address.
l2.addressConflict: Address conflict: {{mac}} also uses {{ip}}. Both network cards stop using it (check it with ipconfig).
l2.addressDefended: {{mac}} also uses {{ip}}. A router interface keeps its address and keeps answering.
l2.cloudProxyArp: {{ip}} is a public address: the provider answers with its own MAC (proxy ARP).
l2.cloudPrivateArp: {{ip}} is not a public address: the provider does not answer.
l2.cloudNeedsDestination: The provider only answers the device that sent to it: without a destination MAC the packet is not sent.
l2.linkDownDrop: Interface {{iface}} has no working link: the packet cannot be sent.
l2.vlanInactive: VLAN {{vlan}} is not in the VLAN database: the switch forwards nothing in it. Create it with 'vlan {{vlan}}'.
l2.unknownSsid: This radio does not offer SSID {{ssid}}: the frame is dropped.
l2.noSubInterface: No sub-interface of {{port}} uses the 802.1Q tag {{vlan}}: the frame is dropped. Add one with 'encapsulation dot1Q {{vlan}}'.
l2.ispNoService: Only a router port gets internet service; the device on {{port}} is not a router.

l3.forThisDevice: The destination {{dst}} is an address of this device.
l3.notRouting: The destination {{dst}} is not an address of this device, and this device does not route: the packet is dropped.
l3.routeFound: Routing table: {{dst}} matches {{prefix}}/{{length}}; next hop {{via}}, out of {{iface}}.
l3.connectedRoute: {{dst}} is in the directly connected network {{prefix}}/{{length}} on {{iface}}.
l3.noRoute: The routing table has no route to {{dst}}: the packet is dropped.
l3.ttlDecremented: The TTL is decremented from {{from}} to {{to}}.
l3.ttlExpired: The TTL reached 0: the packet is dropped and ICMP Time Exceeded is sent to {{src}}.
l3.localNetwork: {{dst}} is in the own network: the packet is sent directly.
l3.viaGateway: {{dst}} is outside the own network: the packet goes to the default gateway {{gateway}}.
l3.gatewayNotSet: {{dst}} is outside the own network and no default gateway is set.
l3.gatewayOutsideSubnet: The default gateway {{gateway}} is not in the own network.
l3.noUsableAddress: The interface has no usable IPv4 address.
l3.echoReplyCreated: An ICMP echo reply is sent back to {{dst}}.
l3.unreachableSent: ICMP Destination Unreachable ({{code}}) is sent to {{dst}}.
l3.privateToInternet: {{dst}} is a private address: the internet does not route it, so the router answers Destination Unreachable.
l3.internetDelivers: {{dst}} is a public address: the internet delivers the packet.
l3.portUnreachable: No service listens on {{protocol}} port {{port}}: ICMP Port Unreachable is sent.
l3.toTransport: The {{protocol}} segment is handed to port {{port}}.
l3.echoTimeout: No answer to echo request {{sequence}} within {{ms}} ms.
l3.broadcastReceived: {{dst}} is a broadcast address: the packet is for every device of the network, this one included.
l3.echoRequestReceived: ICMP echo request {{sequence}} from {{src}}: this device answers it.
l3.echoBroadcastIgnored: An echo request sent to a broadcast address is not answered.
l3.echoReplyStale: ICMP echo reply from {{src}} that no ping waits for any more: it is ignored.
l3.noRoutePublic: The routing table has no route to the public address {{dst}} (no way to the internet): the packet is dropped without an answer.
l3.ispNoRoute: {{dst}} is not a public address: the internet has no route to it and drops the packet.
l3.ispIgnores: The internet answers only ping, DNS and web traffic to public addresses: this packet gets no answer.
l3.tcpReset: Nothing listens on TCP port {{port}}: a TCP RST is sent back.
l3.noIcmpAboutIcmpError: No ICMP error is sent about an ICMP error, a broadcast or a packet without a valid source address.
l3.arpFailedUnreachable: ARP for the next hop {{ip}} failed: ICMP Destination Unreachable (host) goes back to {{dst}}.
l3.arpFailedLocal: ARP for {{ip}} failed on this device: it reports Destination host unreachable from its own address.
l3.loopback: {{dst}} is this device's own address: the packet never leaves the device.
l3.cableDisconnected: The network adapter has no working cable or Wi-Fi connection: the packet cannot be sent.
l3.portDisabled: The network adapter or the switch port it is plugged into is disabled: the packet cannot be sent.
l3.invalidConfig: The IPv4 settings of {{iface}} (address, mask or gateway) are not valid: the packet cannot be sent.
l3.invalidHostAddress: {{ip}} is the network or broadcast address of its subnet: a host cannot send from it.
l3.ipConflict: {{ip}} is used by another device too (duplicate address): this device cannot use it.
l3.invalidDestination: {{dst}} is not a valid IPv4 address.
l3.sendOnInterface: The packet leaves through {{iface}} without a routing table lookup.
l3.tracertProbe: Tracert probe to {{dst}} with TTL {{ttl}}: every router on the way decrements it by one.
l3.timeExceededSent: ICMP Time Exceeded is sent back to {{dst}} from the interface the packet arrived on.

services.dhcpDiscover: DHCP DISCOVER: the client looks for a DHCP server.
services.dhcpRequest: DHCP REQUEST: the client asks for {{ip}}.
services.dhcpNoPool: No DHCP pool serves the network of interface {{iface}}.
services.dhcpPoolExhausted: Pool {{pool}} has no free address left.
services.dhcpRelayed: DHCP relay: the message is forwarded to {{server}}.
services.dnsForwarded: {{name}} is not in the local records: the query is forwarded to {{server}}.
services.tcpRefused: Nothing listens on TCP port {{port}}: the connection is refused (RST).
services.dhcpDiscoverBroadcast: DISCOVER goes from 0.0.0.0 to the broadcast address 255.255.255.255: the client has no address yet and does not know where a server is.
services.dhcpOfferReceived: Offer of {{ip}} from {{server}} received: the first offer wins.
services.dhcpOfferIgnored: The client already took another offer: this one is ignored.
services.dhcpNotForThisClient: The message is for {{mac}}, another client: it is ignored.
services.dhcpRequestBroadcast: The REQUEST is a broadcast too: every server learns which offer the client took.
services.dhcpOtherServer: The client chose server {{server}}: this server withdraws its offer.
services.dhcpTimeout: No DHCP server answered after {{attempts}} attempts.
services.dhcpServiceDisabled: The DHCP service of this device is off: the message is ignored.
services.dhcpNoDhcpNic: No network adapter of this device gets its address from DHCP.
services.dhcpReleaseReceived: {{mac}} gave {{ip}} back; the server keeps the lease record and will offer the same address again.
services.dhcpRelayGiaddr: The relay writes its own address {{giaddr}} into giaddr: the server picks the pool of that network and answers the relay.
services.dhcpRelayToClient: DHCP relay: the server's answer is broadcast on {{iface}}, the client's network.
services.dnsNotSet: No DNS server is configured: the name cannot be resolved.
services.dnsInvalidServer: {{server}} is not a valid IPv4 address: the next DNS server is tried.
services.dnsCacheHit: {{name}} is in the DNS cache ({{ip}}): no query is sent.
services.dnsCacheNegative: The DNS cache remembers that {{name}} does not exist: no query is sent.
services.dnsRecordFound: {{name}} is a record of this server: it answers {{ip}} itself.
services.dnsNoForwarders: {{name}} is not in the records and no forwarder is set: the server answers that the name does not exist (NXDOMAIN).
services.dnsLoop: This server is already forwarding {{name}}: the query came back in a loop and is dropped.
services.dnsPublicResolver: {{server}} is a public resolver on the internet: it looks the name up.
services.dnsNotAResolver: No DNS server runs at {{ip}}: the query is dropped and the client waits in vain.
services.dnsNoService: {{server}} answered ICMP port unreachable: no DNS service runs there.
services.dnsServerUnreachable: {{server}} cannot be reached: the next DNS server is tried.
services.dnsForwardTimeout: Forwarder {{server}} did not answer in time.
services.dnsForwardFailed: No forwarder answered for {{name}}: the server gives up without answering.
services.dnsForwardAnswer: The forwarder's answer is passed back to the client {{client}}.
services.httpTimeout: No HTTP answer from {{host}} within {{ms}} ms.
services.httpUnreachable: {{ip}} cannot be reached: the browser gives up.
services.httpPageMissing: The web server has no page {{path}}: 404 Not Found.
services.tcpConnectionRefused: The server refused the connection (TCP RST).
services.tcpClose: TCP FIN: the connection is closed.
services.staleReply: Nobody waits for this answer any more: it is ignored.
